messages.author: b5b95ffe4c13847b
messages.subject: Compiling error in example on page 95 of Stan Reference Manual v. 2.2.0
parts:
Dear Community,
I am trying to run the example model for a multivariate (hierarchical) regression on page 95 of the Reference Manual for Stan version 2.2.0 but I am running into a compiling error.

This is the error message returned when calling stan():

TRANSLATING MODEL 'fullmodel' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  : 
  failed to parse Stan model 'fullmodel' with error message:
EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION: file=input; line=27, column=57

beta[j] ~ multi_normal((u[j] * gamma)’, Sigma_beta);
                                                        ^-- here
DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
no matches for function name="multi_normal_log"
    arg 0 type=vector
    arg 1 type=row vector
    arg 2 type=matrix
available function signatures for multi_normal_log:
0.  multi_normal_log(vector, vector, matrix) : real
unknown distribution=multi_normal
Parser expecting: <eps>

I have actually slightly modified the code to fit a logistic rather than a linear model but I doubt this is the problem. Here is the modified code (note commented out lines):
fullmodel<- '
data {
int<lower=0> N; // num individuals
int<lower=1> K; // num ind predictors
int<lower=1> J; // num groups
int<lower=1> L; // num group predictors
int<lower=1,upper=J> jj[N]; // group for individual
matrix[N,K] x; // individual predictors
matrix[J,L] u; // group predictors
vector[N] y; // outcomes
}
parameters {
corr_matrix[K] Omega; // prior covariance
vector<lower=0>[K] tau; // prior scale
matrix[L,K] gamma; // group coeffs
vector[K] beta[J]; // indiv coeffs by group
#real<lower=0> sigma; // prediction error scale of the original linear model (commented out)
}
model {
matrix[K,K] Sigma_beta;
Sigma_beta <- diag_matrix(tau) * Omega * diag_matrix(tau);
tau ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
Omega ~ lkj_corr(2);
for (l in 1:L)
gamma[l] ~ normal(0,5);
for (j in 1:J)
beta[j] ~ multi_normal((u[j] * gamma)’, Sigma_beta);
for (n in 1:N)
#y[n] ~ normal(x[n] * beta[jj[n]], sigma); // original linear predictor commented out
y[n] ~ bernoulli(inv_logit(x[n] * beta[jj[n]]));
}
'
I am using R version 3.0.2 (2013-09-25) in Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit) and rstan_2.2.0.
Info on the compiler is:
> system("g++ --version")
G__~1.EXE (GCC) 4.6.3 20111208 (prerelease)

Is this really an error in the manual? Or what can I be doing wrong?
Thanks for any guidance.
Edwin
P.S. Explanations for beginners are highly appreciated.

messages.author: ca51dc784e0edba6
messages.subject: Re: Compiling error in example on page 95 of Stan Reference Manual v. 2.2.0
parts:
your error is in data block.

when you sample a random number from bernoulli distribution, the left hand side should be int. However, your code is

which implicitly assume real values.

Therefore, you should modify your code like

data {
int<lower=0> N; // num individuals
int<lower=1> K; // num ind predictors
int<lower=1> J; // num groups
int<lower=1> L; // num group predictors
int<lower=1,upper=J> jj[N]; // group for individual
matrix[N,K] x; // individual predictors
matrix[J,L] u; // group predictors

# you have a typo here.
#vector[N] y; // outcomes
int y[N];
}

The error massage is kinda misreading. I spent a little bit of time to debug your code.

Hi,
You are both right. I´ll recap to clarify.
There were two errors in my code. I reported the first one in my original mail was it was related indeed to the arguments to multi-normal. It seems I was using an unrecognized prime character (by R or stan? I don't know) to transpose (u[j] * gamma). I solved it by chance after unsuccessfully trying the change suggested by Soga ("the idea fell form sky"... hope the expression translates correctly to English).
Soga detected the second error in my code which would have popped as an error if I would have not changed the code as Soga suggested. 
In short the error messages thrown by stan seem correct. 
At the end I copy the error message I get when I run the model with the first problem corrected but without fixing the definition of y.

Many thanks for your input. Now I can go on exploring stan.
Edwin
